Thanks Marissa — great note and clear plan. I filled a few items inline below and attached a short traffic summary. A couple answers:

- Baseline RPS: 4–6 RPS during typical daytime hours (our clinic cluster).
- Burst patterns: up to ~55 RPS for short bursts (1–3 minutes) during morning intake windows; we also see a few sustained bursts ~30 RPS for 10–15 minutes during shift changes.
- Typical token lengths: prompts average ~60 tokens, responses average ~160 tokens; max observed combined tokens ~800 (rare).
- Concurrency: typically 8–12 concurrent clinical sessions that may trigger parallel requests; peak concurrent jobs ~25 across our region during busiest windows.
- Residency: US-only data routing required.

Success criteria (clarifying):
- Clinical quality: >= 85% agreement with clinician-provided summaries on the pilot evaluation set.
- Latency: p95 < 500ms for representative requests measured from our ingress to the model response (includes network).
- Reliability: no more than 1% error/timeout rate during the two-week trial.

Timeline: the proposed weeks work for us; procurement will need 2–3 business days for an NDA. Please share the workload template and SE contact.

Thanks for the context — this looks straightforward to scope. High-level SE notes and proposed config: 

Initial recommendation:
- Model: rwd-open-summarize-v2 (balanced quality/cost). If Acme needs max quality, we'll run a small eval vs. rwd-open-summarize-v3.
- Quantization: 4-bit Q4_0 for baseline; can move to Q8 if quality gaps appear.
- Deployment: Hosted dedicated pool (US region) with autoscale + burst capacity.

Sizing assumptions (based on Alex numbers):
- Typical request profile: median 60 tokens prompt + 160 tokens response = ~220 tokens/request.
- Baseline throughput: 6 RPS steady; peak bursts to 55 RPS for short windows.
- Concurrency: plan for 12 steady concurrent, 25 peak concurrent.

Performance and tuning notes:
- Batch sizing: use dynamic batching up to 8 requests/batch for steady traffic; during bursts we allow smaller batches to preserve latency.
- KV cache: enabled for session-based interactions; reduces compute for repeated prefixes. 
- Expected latency: p95 ~ 220–420ms for median requests on a 1x high-throughput GPU instance when batching is effective; during extreme bursts p95 could approach 500–650ms unless we scale burst pool.
- Autoscale: enable fast scale-up policy with warm standby capacity to handle 1–3 minute spikes; recommend 20% reserved burst capacity for morning windows.

Success criteria mapping:
- Quality: we'll run the customer eval set during the first week and provide an automated scorecard; if quality < 85% we’ll switch to the v3 model for the evaluation cohort.
- Latency: target p95 < 500ms; we’ll instrument with tracing and provide token-level cost/latency breakdowns in the console.
- Reliability: plan to keep error rate <1% — we’ll set retries and circuit-breakers as part of the test harness.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Customer returns completed workload_profile_template.xlsx and sample eval set.
2) Redwood SE runs a quick internal sizing test and returns a recommended Dedicated pool config + estimated cost for the 2-week trial (by Apr 16).
3) Kickoff call week of Apr 19 to exchange access and confirm eval logistics.
